Under the earlier system of taxation, credit of taxes being levied by Central Government was not available as set-off for payment of taxes levied by State Governments, and vice versa. Which of the following statement/s is/are correct?
1. ITC means the credit of Input Tax on the supplies of goods and services or both received by a registered person.
2. Eligibility of ITC which may be as under-taxable supply, non-taxable supply, zero-rated supply.
Select the correct answer using the code given below-
Code :
x: Uninterrupted and seamless chain of input tax credit (ITC) is one of the key features of Goods and Services Tax. ITC is a mechanism to avoid cascading of taxes. Any registered person can avail credit of tax paid on the inward supply of goods or services or both, which is used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of business subject to certain conditions. Thus, ITC means the credit of input tax on the supplies of goods and services or both received by a registered person. Eligibility of ITC includes taxable supply and zerorated supply, but non-taxable, exempt and nil-rated supplies are not eligible for ITC. Zero-rated supply is different from nil-rated supply (goods and services on which 0% GST is applicable). Any supplies made by a registered dealer as an export (both goods or services) or supply to an SEZ qualifies for zero-rated supplies in GST and ITC is available for them. Hence, statement 1 is correct while statement 2 is incorrect.

o: Any Union loan or guarantee is outstanding

s: Which Article is associated with grants for any public purpose chosen by the executive?
x: Article 282 covers grants for any public purpose; Article 275 grants are for States in need, ST welfare and Scheduled Areas.

Plan grants continued after the Planning Commission was abolished in 2015

s: On which fund are statutory grants-in-aid under Article 275 charged?
x: Article 275 grants, recommended by the Finance Commission, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India; Article 282 grants are voted.

s: Article 275 grants-in-aid are specially meant for which of the following?
o: Welfare of Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Areas
x: Article 275 statutory grants go to States in need, including for welfare of Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Areas.

s: What was the principal feature of the 'grand bargain' proposed by the 16th Finance Commission in relation to cesses?
o: All cesses would be transferred directly to local bodies
States would accept a smaller share of a larger pool if most cesses were merged into regular taxes
States would receive a larger share of a smaller pool without any change in cesses
States would impose all Union cesses within their territories
x: The proposal envisaged States taking a smaller share of a larger pool if the Centre merged most cesses into regular taxes.

s: The amount of cesses and surcharges per ₹100 of Central tax was at a decade high in which year and at what level?
x: Cesses and surcharges amounted to ₹13.5 per ₹100 of Central tax in 2021–22, described as a decade high. The estimate for 2025–26 was ₹11.

s: What was the approximate effective devolution to the States as a percentage of gross tax revenue, despite the headline 41% share of the divisible pool?
x: Because cesses and surcharges are outside the divisible pool, the effective devolution was approximately 30–32% of gross tax revenue, lower than the headline 41% of the divisible pool.

s: Which of the following is excluded from the divisible pool under Article 270?
x: Cesses and surcharges lie outside the Article 270 divisible pool, so they are not shared with States.

s: Which of the following aggravates vertical fiscal imbalance between the Centre and States?
o: Cesses and surcharges kept outside the divisible pool
Removal of conditionalities on Centrally Sponsored Schemes
Retention of independent indirect taxes by States
x: Cesses and surcharges, loss of independent indirect taxes to GST, CSS conditionalities and weak State revenue all aggravate the imbalance.

s: What is the basic cause of vertical fiscal imbalance in India?
o: States have larger and more buoyant tax bases than the Union
The Union holds the larger and more buoyant tax bases such as corporation tax, income tax and most of GST
Local bodies collect most of the tax revenue in the country
The Finance Commission fixes the expenditure of States
x: Vertical fiscal imbalance arises because the Union controls the larger, more buoyant tax bases (corporation tax, income tax, most of GST) while States carry heavy spending duties. A reverses the position, C is wrong because local bodies collect little, and the Finance Commission does not fix State expenditure (D).

s: Which government set up the Rajamannar Committee (1969), which advocated greater State autonomy?
x: The Tamil Nadu Government constituted the Rajamannar Committee in 1969; it argued for greater State autonomy and more resources.

s: During which period did the Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State relations function?
x: The Sarkaria Commission sat during 1983–1988; the Rajamannar Committee dates to 1969 and the Punchhi Commission to 2007–2010.

s: On whose recommendation was the Inter-State Council under Article 263 set up in 1990?
x: The Union-appointed Sarkaria Commission's recommendations led to the Inter-State Council in 1990.

s: Who chaired the Commission on Centre-State Relations of 2007-10?
x: The Punchhi Commission (2007-10) was chaired by Justice M.M. Punchhi; Sarkaria was 1983-88.

s: Who chaired the Commission on Centre-State Relations set up in 1983?
x: Justice R.S. Sarkaria chaired the 1983-88 Commission; its report led to the Inter-State Council (1990).

s: Revenue Deficit Grants to Andhra Pradesh are given under which Article of the Constitution?
x: AP receives Revenue Deficit Grants under Article 275, along with CSS funds, local body grants and SDLs raised through the RBI.

s: Through which institution does Andhra Pradesh raise its State Development Loans?
x: AP raises SDLs through the RBI.
